papers.title: Towards ontology driven learning of visual concept detectors
papers.abstract: The maturity of deep learning techniques has led in recent years to a breakthrough in object recognition in visual media. While for some specific benchmarks, neural techniques seem to match if not outperform human judgement, challenges are still open for detecting arbitrary concepts in arbitrary videos. In this paper, we propose a system that combines neural techniques, a large scale visual concepts ontology, and an active learning loop, to provide on the fly model learning of arbitrary concepts. We give an overview of the system as a whole, and focus on the central role of the ontology for guiding and bootstrapping the learning of new concepts, improving the recall of concept detection, and, on the user end, providing semantic search on a library of annotated videos.

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on visual concept detection using ontology and active learning, with no mention of finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanics applications.

summary_en.motivation: To enable on-the-fly learning of arbitrary visual concepts by leveraging an ontological structure to guide detection.
summary_en.method: The system integrates deep neural networks, a large-scale visual concept ontology, and an active learning loop to bootstrap concept detectors.
summary_en.result: The ontology plays a central role in guiding new concept learning, improving recall, and enabling semantic search over annotated videos.
summary_en.validation: The paper provides a system overview without detailed experimental validation on specific benchmarks.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization under mixed constraints with a slack-variable augmented Lagrangian
papers.abstract: An augmented Lagrangian (AL) can convert a constrained optimization problem into a sequence of simpler (e.g., unconstrained) problems, which are then usually solved with local solvers. Recently, surrogate-based Bayesian optimization (BO) sub-solvers have been successfully deployed in the AL framework for a more global search in the presence of inequality constraints; however, a drawback was that expected improvement (EI) evaluations relied on Monte Carlo. Here we introduce an alternative slack variable AL, and show that in this formulation the EI may be evaluated with library routines. The slack variables furthermore facilitate equality as well as inequality constraints, and mixtures thereof. We show how our new slack "ALBO" compares favorably to the original. Its superiority over conventional alternatives is reinforced on several mixed constraint examples.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法提出了一种结合松弛变量增广拉格朗日与贝叶斯优化的约束优化方法，可用于解决昂贵仿真中的混合约束问题，虽未涉及生物力学，但方法具有迁移潜力。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA simulations, implant biomechanics, or any biomedical validation; it focuses on algorithmic development for constrained BO on synthetic test functions.

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently handle mixed equality and inequality constraints in expensive black-box optimization.
summary_en.method: Introduces a slack-variable augmented Lagrangian within a Bayesian optimization framework with analytical expected improvement.
summary_en.result: Outperforms previous AL-based BO and conventional methods on mixed constraint benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Numerical tests on several standard constrained optimization problems.

papers.title: Selective laser melting additive manufacturing of in situ Al <sub>2</sub> Si <sub>4</sub> O <sub>10</sub> /Al composites: Microstructural characteristics and mechanical properties
papers.abstract: The advanced selective laser melting technology was employed to prepare in situ Al based composites. Relationship among selective laser melting processing parameters, microstructures and resultant mechanical properties had been established. It turned out that in situ Al 2 Si 4 O 10 /Al composites were successfully fabricated by selective laser melting of Al 2 O 3 /AlSi10Mg composite powders. Due to the overlap between neighboring tracks and the remelting of previously solidified layers, two distinguished zones consisting of track core and track overlap were produced in laser induced melt pool. The two zones, respectively experienced different thermal histories, thus leading to the variation of cooling rate, which had a significant influence on the microstructural development and resultant mechanical performances. The track core mainly consisted of remarkably refined cellular dendritic Al matrix decorated with uniformly distributed ring-structured Al 2 Si 4 O 10 reinforcements, while the track overlap was characterized with comparatively coarse columnar dendritic Al matrix as well as the coarse Al 2 Si 4 O 10 reinforcements. At the optimal v of 500 mm/s, the obtained dynamic nanohardness ( H d ) of track core ( H d = 3.79 GPa) and track overlap ( H d = 3.52 GPa) for selective laser melting processed composites part both showed tremendous enhancement upon that of unreinforced Al part ( H d = 0.58 GPa). The dry sliding wear tests indicated that the optimally prepared Al 2 Si 4 O 10 /Al composites part exhibited excellent wear performance with a considerably low coefficient of friction of 0.32 and a significantly reduced wear rate of 4.52 × 10 −5 mm 3 N −1 m −1 . The formed consecutive protective adherent tribolayer on the worn surface and the significantly enhanced hardness of the composites well accounted for the superior wear performance.

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate in-situ Al2Si4O10/Al composites via selective laser melting and establish the relationship between processing parameters, microstructure, and mechanical properties.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting of Al2O3/AlSi10Mg composite powders to form in-situ reinforcements, with analysis of track overlap and core regions.
summary_en.result: Optimal scanning speed of 500 mm/s yielded composites with nanohardness up to 3.79 GPa and a low coefficient of friction of 0.32 with a wear rate of 4.52 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties validated through nanoindentation and dry sliding wear tests.
